Kuznica Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Kuźnica, Poland

Not demolished. Jews are first recorded in Kuźnica in the 16th century, growing to 450 (42%) by 1921, mostly murdered during WWII. This cemetery, possibly established when the town's independent Jewish community formed in the 17th-18th centuries, fell into disrepair postwar - used as pasture and a gravel mine, with a power line built through it. A 1981 government survey found no fence, overturned tombstones, and the site fully overtaken by self-seeded plants, recording its last burial as 1945; a 1994 Grodno-Białystok road was built through its eastern section. A 1989-1996 fence with menorah motifs now protects part of the grounds.
